groups.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

parts.context: A coordinator describes activities, rooms and volunteering opportunities at a community centre.

transcript.text: Good evening, and thank you all for coming to our annual open evening at the Brookfield Community Centre. My name is Samuel Osei, and I coordinate the programme. Tonight I want to tell you what's available, and how you can get involved.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: The centre has been part of this neighbourhood for over forty years. It began as a small youth club, and today more than a thousand people use it every month, from toddlers to pensioners.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: Many of our volunteers first came here as users, and when they found how much they enjoyed it, they decided to give something back.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: Let me start with the groups, because each has its own room. The chess club, which is very popular with retired people, meets in the Oak Room, upstairs, where it's quiet and there's plenty of natural light.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: The sewing and knitting group has recently moved. It used to be in the Oak Room, but it now meets in the Willow Room, which has long tables and better lighting, and that suits their work much better.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: Our young people's drama group rehearses in the main hall, because it has a stage. They're preparing a new production for spring, and they're always happy to welcome new members aged between twelve and sixteen.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: The community choir, which sings everything from folk songs to pop, uses the Studio. It's the only room with a piano, and the walls are sound-proofed, so the neighbours don't complain.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: And finally, the gardening club works in the Courtyard Garden at the back. They grow vegetables and herbs, which they share with members, and a few years ago they won a regional prize for their design.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: Now, about membership. It costs twelve pounds a year, and this includes access to all the groups. Pensioners and students pay half that, and no one is turned away because they cannot afford it.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: Next, volunteering, which keeps the centre running. We have around sixty volunteers, and we're particularly short of people to help at the reception desk in the mornings, which is busy from nine until noon.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: We also need drivers for our lunch club. Every Wednesday we deliver hot meals to elderly people who cannot leave their homes, and for many of them, the driver is the only visitor they have that day.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: If you would like to volunteer, you'll need to complete a short background check, which takes about two weeks, and then you'll attend a training evening, where we explain our safety rules and how to support people with disabilities.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: Looking ahead, our biggest project this year is a new accessible entrance. At the moment, the building has steps at the front, which is a problem for wheelchair users and parents with pushchairs. The work will begin in September.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI

transcript.text: We're raising money for it, and so far we have reached about two thirds of the target. Anything you can give will make a real difference. Thank you, and please enjoy the refreshments in the hall.
transcript.speaker: MR OSEI
